title: Readiness Estimator: Black Hole Starships
definition: Estimates Black Hole Starships readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Black Hole Starships components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a singularity hull that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where Hawking reactors monitoring, radiation propulsion redundancy, or containment fields maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Black Hole Starships Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Black Hole Starships: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Black Hole Starships — theoretical ships powered by artificial microscopic black holes.

Phase 1 — Prove (Hawking reactors): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (radiation propulsion): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (containment fields): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (power extraction): singularity hull as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and deep-space-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
